source.title: A symbolic-connectionist theory of relational inference and generalization

confidence_rationale: LISA is the canonical argument that analogical mapping requires DEDICATED machinery -- dynamic role-filler binding via temporal synchrony -- rather than emerging from distributed representations alone. That is the strongest principled case for the 'separate operator' horn of Q-074, i.e. for building MECH-421 explicitly. Discounted because it is a 2003 cognitive-architecture theory whose 'binding must be dedicated' premise has been partially challenged by later high-dimensional and attention-based models; and because 'requires dedicated binding' does not strictly rule out that MECH-300 traversal already supplies such binding.
failure_signatures: LISA's dynamic binding is inherently capacity-limited (roughly 4-6 role bindings, 2-3 propositions at once) because synchrony can represent bindings at only one hierarchical level at a time -- if analogy needs a dedicated binder, REE inherits that working-memory bottleneck as a hard constraint, not an incidental one.

If REE expects analogy to emerge from MECH-300 traversal but the LISA thesis is right that structure-sensitive mapping needs explicit variable binding, an emergent stack would produce systematic binding errors (illusory conjunctions, role confusions) on exactly the hard analogies that motivate having the mechanism.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Structure-sensitive relational inference and analogical mapping require dynamic binding of roles to fillers (implemented in LISA via temporal synchrony), giving a system both connectionist flexibility and symbolic structure-sensitivity; this dedicated binding mechanism is what makes analogy work, and it is inherently capacity-limited.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-074's first horn says analogy (MECH-421) should be built as a distinct operator over the relational stack. LISA is the principled defence of that horn: relational mapping is not free -- it needs an explicit binder to keep 'who plays which role' straight across the two analogues, and distributed representations without such a binder cannot maintain structure. For REE, this argues MECH-421 warrants dedicated variable-binding machinery rather than being left to emerge from MECH-419/MECH-420.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The theory establishes that analogy needs a binder; it does not establish that MECH-300 cognitive-map traversal cannot itself BE that binder. If traversal over the shared symbolic map already implements role-filler binding, the 'dedicated operator' and 'emergent from traversal' horns partially converge, and LISA weakens the pure-emergence reading without settling the build decision. LISA is also a psychological model of human analogy, a transfer step away from REE's substrate.
mapping.source_context: Symbolic-connectionist cognitive architecture; simulations of analogical access, mapping, inference, and schema induction, with the binding mechanism as the load-bearing commitment.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, highly-cited theory (source_quality 0.85). mapping_fidelity is only moderate because 'analogy needs binding' does not cleanly decide 'build a separate module vs. traversal supplies binding'; it weakens pure emergence more than it proves a bolted-on operator.
